profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded technology company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trading on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA. The company reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, as filed in its most recent 10-K with the SEC under CIK 0001045810. Its website focuses on artificial intelligence infrastructure, with particular emphasis on foundation models and deployment tooling for enterprise customers.

The company's primary AI model offering is NVIDIA Nemotron, which it describes as a family of multimodal, open models built for agentic AI applications including reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, neural machine translation, and multimodal vision tasks. The site highlights Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a variant oriented toward faster specialized task completion, and NeMo Switchyard as a routing layer for directing agent steps to appropriate models. NVIDIA states that model weights, training datasets, and training techniques are published openly under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA. The company also offers Nemotron models packaged as NVIDIA NIM microservices, a second tracked product, for enterprise deployment requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, with deployment supported on platforms including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark and tooling including NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, and vLLM.

The held facts indicate NVIDIA has a notable legal exposure profile in California, with 161 cases associated with that jurisdiction, though no specific litigation details are recorded in the current data.
